chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: 'Supplication is the weapon of the believer, and the pillar of the religion, and the light of the heavens and the earth.'

key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a — supplication or prayer addressed directly to God, distinct from formal ritual prayer (salat)
key_terms.سلاح: Weapon — means of defense and empowerment; here signifying that supplication protects and strengthens the believer
key_terms.عمود الدين: Pillar of the religion — foundational support; the metaphor of a tent pole suggests du'a holds up the entire structure of religion
key_terms.نور السماوات والأرض: Light of the heavens and the earth — echoes the famous 'Light Verse' (Nur, 24:35); supplication is a cosmic light permeating all of creation

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the importance of supplication (du'a) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in which du'a (supplication) is described with three profound metaphors: a weapon, a pillar, and a light. This hadith elevates supplication to a central spiritual practice — not merely a ritual act, but the believer's primary means of engaging with the divine. The original audience of this teaching were the early Shia community in Medina and Kufa who lived under political oppression, and the metaphor of supplication as a 'weapon' would have resonated deeply as a means of spiritual resistance and reliance on God.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The supplication is a weapon of the Momin and a pillar of the Religion, and a Light of the skies and the earth’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Pleading before Allah for help is believing people’s weapons, the pillar of religion and the light of the heavens and earth.’”
